clue.text: Timer almost jammed, causing alert

parts.note: a watch is a timer worn on the wrist

indicators.note: almost says the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: jammed means packed full

explanation.surface: A clock nearly stuck makes someone wary.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone alert keeps a close eye on things, so they are vigilant and observant.

clue.text: Cautious about Catholic slogan

indicators.note: about means the cautious word surrounds the abbreviation

parts.note: wary means cautious
RC is Roman Catholic

explanation.surface: Careful around a Catholic catchphrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A rallying cry or catchphrase used by a group is figuratively its battle shout.

clue.text: In Serengeti, grisly river!

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the following words

explanation.surface: A grim river in the African Serengeti.
explanation.walkthrough: The Serengeti suggests an African river, but this one flows through Turkey and Iraq.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the great Mesopotamian waterway paired with the Euphrates.

clue.text: Chair to set out that comes in a pod

indicators.note: set out means arranged, so these letters are laid out anew

explanation.surface: Putting out a chair, then something in a pod.
explanation.definitionFit: A haricot is a type of bean, and beans grow inside pods.

clue.text: Low plants develop during thunder burst

indicators.note: during says the develop word sits inside the scrambled letters
burst means broken apart, so these letters are scattered

parts.note: to grow is to develop

explanation.surface: Shrubs spring up in a thunderstorm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burst' rearranges THUNDER into UNDERTH; 'during' puts GROW in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Dense shrubs and bushes growing beneath trees form low vegetation.

clue.text: Train for Rugby, say

definitions.meaning: to train is to teach or drill someone
Rugby is a famous English public ..., given as an example

explanation.surface: Coaching someone for a rugby match.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby looks like the sport, but here it is the English boarding school in the town of that name, where the game is said to have begun.
explanation.definitionFit: To train someone is to educate them; Rugby is one instance of a place of education.

clue.text: Third character on the radio's a proper idiot

definitions.meaning: C, the third letter, is spoken this way in the radio alphabet
a British informal word for a fool

explanation.walkthrough: In the NATO phonetic alphabet used on radio, C is said as this name; in Britain it also means a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: The radio code word for the letter C doubles as British slang for a silly person.

clue.text: Publicly known to be working with criminal history

parts.note: on means working, like a machine switched on
a criminal record is someone's history of offences

explanation.surface: Known to be active with a past conviction.
explanation.definitionFit: Something said openly and officially documented is publicly stated.

clue.text: Kind of policy that's unlikely to appeal to schoolchildren

definitions.text: that's unlikely to appeal to schoolchildren
definitions.meaning: pupils would not welcome an extended school session

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is cryptic: read as two words, it is a lengthy school session.
explanation.definitionFit: A strategy planned for the distant future is described this way; read literally it is a lengthy school period.

clue.text: Art grade for modelling in fashion industry

indicators.note: modelling means shaping something, so these letters are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: An art mark earned for modelling work in the world of fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: The rag trade is an informal name for the business of making and selling clothes.

clue.text: Woman formerly seen around hospital floor covering right leg

parts.note: a mat covers part of a floor
on is the leg side in cricket

explanation.surface: A woman spotted near a hospital in the past, with a rug over her right leg.
explanation.walkthrough: ON = leg is a cricket convention: the leg side of the field is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior nursing officer in charge of a hospital was formerly given this title.

clue.text: There's no end of bother behind bar in American's carriage

indicators.note: behind puts the shortened word after the bar

parts.note: a rail is a bar

indicators.note: no end of says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to bother is to care

explanation.definitionFit: A self-propelled railway passenger vehicle is called this in American usage.

clue.text: Criminal, evil one goes to city having forsaken east end

parts.note: ill means evil, as in ill will
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: in an across entry the east end is the right-hand end, so the word drops its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wicked villain heads for town and leaves London's East End behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East end' suggests London's East End, but in an across word east is the right-hand side, so the final letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something criminal is unlawful, forbidden by law.

clue.text: One is late paying this tax

definitions.text: One is late paying this tax

parts.words: One is late paying this tax
parts.note: late means dead, so this levy is paid on an estate after its owner dies

explanation.walkthrough: 'late' suggests overdue payment, but it means deceased: this British tax falls on a dead person's estate.
explanation.definitionFit: This British tax is charged on what passes to heirs from a deceased person's estate.

clue.text: Champion who opens Olympics?

definitions.meaning: a champion of a cause is its leading advocate
the person carrying the flame lights the cauldron at the opening ceremony

explanation.walkthrough: 'Champion' suggests a winning athlete, but it means a leading campaigner.
explanation.definitionFit: A prominent supporter of a cause is figuratively its standard-carrier, and literally one brings the flame to the Games.

clue.text: Discover second donkey in the open air

parts.note: moke is British slang for a donkey
out means outdoors

explanation.surface: Find another donkey out in the fields.
explanation.walkthrough: MOKE is an old British slang word for a donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: To force something hidden into view, as smoke drives an animal from its burrow, is to uncover it.

clue.text: Borderline cheek that is going over rector's head

indicators.note: in a down entry, going over places the earlier pieces above the next one

parts.note: front means cheek or nerve
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: head says to take the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Nearly outrageous cheek passing over the rector's head.
explanation.definitionFit: The border line between two regions or countries marks their edge.

clue.text: Take note of this: scores must embrace I say!

parts.note: marks are scores, as in an exam
my word and I say are both exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: A teacher's warning: the marks have to include the phrase I say!
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom used to tell someone to listen and remember what is said.

clue.text: Various trams circuiting east — ring for conductor

indicators.note: circuiting says the rearranged letters go around the east letter
various means assorted, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Different trams going round the east, with a ring for the driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conductor' suggests the tram's ticket collector, but it is the orchestra's leader; 'Various' signals the anagram and 'circuiting' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A conductor of an orchestra is given this honorific, Italian for master.

clue.text: A few part with a pound

parts.note: to part is to sever
L stands for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A handful separate with a pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: Some, more than two but not many, makes a small number.

clue.text: Group of trees, old inside and hollow

indicators.note: inside says the old letter goes within the trees word

parts.note: a grove is a small wood

explanation.surface: A copse with an old hollow in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A groove is a long narrow channel or hollow cut into a surface.

clue.text: Young woman raised south of Virginia as servant

indicators.note: south of in a down entry places the turned word below the state

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

indicators.note: raised in a down entry means the word is written upwards

parts.note: a lass is a young woman

explanation.surface: A girl brought up in the American South as a servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A feudal subordinate owing service to a lord, hence a servant or underling.

clue.text: In Scotland, know and name the corrupt man

parts.note: ken is Scots for know

indicators.note: corrupt means spoilt, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A Scot is aware and identifies the dishonest fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name is a crossword's usual way to clue a male forename.

clue.text: Tax returns earn free accommodation in Greece

indicators.note: returns means the tax word is read backwards

parts.note: VAT is value added tax

indicators.note: free means loose, so these letters are let out of order

explanation.surface: Tax rebates get you free lodging in Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns VAT into TAV; 'free' rearranges EARN into ERNA.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek tavern or small restaurant, often with rooms, offering lodging and food to visitors.

clue.text: Drug work I polished off

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
to polish off food is to eat it all, so ate

explanation.surface: A narcotic: I finished the job.
explanation.definitionFit: An opium-derived narcotic is a drug, often a painkiller.

clue.text: Jumbo-sized portion of chicken or moussaka

indicators.note: portion of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A huge helping of chicken or moussaka.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumbo-sized means huge, as large as an elephant.

clue.text: Attack unexpectedly and get going

definitions.meaning: to start a machine by flicking a switch

explanation.surface: Ambush someone and then set off.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to round on someone and to switch something into action.

clue.text: What a surprise — both sides fit

indicators.note: both sides means the word appears on each side, twice over

parts.note: fit means healthy, well

explanation.surface: Astonishment that something fits on either side.
explanation.definitionFit: The doubled exclamation is a set phrase expressing surprise.
